text:
Calgary's problem is not bad luck. At 11-14-2, with 24 points and a 7% playoff chance by our simulations, the Flames are roughly where their play says they should be: 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances on both sides), and a points total almost exactly matching what their chances earned. They give up 3.35 expected goals an hour and create 2.75. That is a rebuilding team's profile, and the standings agree.

Friday's 5-3 loss in New Jersey was the season in miniature. Devin Cooley kept them in it early, Zach Whitecloud gave them a third-period lead, and then the Devils, who had out-chanced them 3.88 expected goals to 2.33, took it back. The injuries haven't helped: Martin Pospisil has been the most written-about Flame for the wrong reasons, and Morgan Frost, a pending free agent the Calgary Herald is already asking questions about, missed Wednesday's game.

The bright spots are young. Zayne Parekh and Yan Kuznetsov have 53% of the expected goals as a pair, the one regular unit of theirs on the right side of the chances, and Jonathan Castagna's goal after a staredown with his idol Sidney Crosby was the feel-good night of the month (he is running hot, four points in ten on 3.1 expected). Watch how much the kids play, and whether Frost's name starts showing up in trade talk.
